changelog: Insert a single narrow binding rule: keep a noun/verb head with an immediately following numeral/quantity/unit/date/parenthetical measure to avoid detaching measurements that cause incoherence (addresses the primary_finding).
findings: The prompt underrates cuts that separate a predicate (verb or clause head) from the phrase that completes its meaning, causing detached predicates or mis-scoped modifiers when pieces are translated independently.

The prompt mishandles numeric/measurement attachments: it allows cuts that detach numerals, units, dates or parenthetical measures from the noun or phrase they quantify, which produces incoherence or contradiction when pieces are translated separately.

edits.now: - Keep a noun or verb head together with an immediately following numeral, quant

diagnosis.why: Inserting the narrow head+measurement binding made the model avoid cuts that separate a noun/verb head from an immediately following numeral/quantity, so many very-short pieces (≤3 and ≤5-word pieces) improved because measurements stayed attached to their heads. However that binding pushed cuts elsewhere (isolating determiners/pronouns or breaking enumerations) and produced small net harm over full sentences (≤99), so the overall H_set change is slightly negative and not significant.
diagnosis.lesson: When adding a binding to keep heads with immediately following numerals, ensure it doesn't force cuts that create single-word fragments or split coordinate/enumeration structure, since the rule helps very short pieces but can worsen longer-piece coherence.
